# 03 A subgraph groups the nodes inside it

## Outcome

`subgraph Ingest ... end` draws a titled frame around the nodes declared inside it, and nesting
works.

## Why this ticket exists

Every real Mermaid flowchart past a dozen nodes groups them, and Siren refuses the keyword outright.
It is one corpus row and far more than one row's worth of documents.

**A port again, and the same one.** `layoutDirectedGraph` already does clusters — `parentId` and
`isCluster`, with compound mode switched on **only when a cluster is declared** so that a graph
without one keeps the exact placement it had. Class-diagram namespaces have used that path since
the class board. Read `layoutClassDiagram`'s namespace handling first.

It also carries a trap that ticket already hit: **a cluster's id must be prefixed.**
`layoutClassDiagram` uses `namespace:${id}` because a namespace may legitimately be named after a
class. A subgraph may legitimately be named after a node, so it needs the same guard for the same
reason — and `generatedId(kind, n)` plus ADR-0010 is where this repo settled how such ids are
spelled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `subgraph Title ... end` parses; the nodes declared inside it belong to it; the frame is drawn
      with its title.
- [ ] **Nesting works** — a subgraph inside a subgraph. Assert at two levels, because one level can
      be made to work by an implementation that cannot nest.
- [ ] A subgraph named the same as a node does not collide. Assert it; this is the trap the class
      diagram already paid for.
- [ ] An edge crossing a subgraph boundary routes correctly, and an edge between two subgraphs does
      too. Assert both — this is what compound layout is for and what a naive implementation gets
      wrong.
- [ ] **Measure with the probe** what Mermaid does with `direction LR` written *inside* a subgraph,
      and decide in or out. If out, refuse it explicitly rather than ignoring it — an ignored
      direction is a silent mis-render, which the corpus would have to record. Say which you chose.
- [ ] A subgraph is a timeline target and takes an author style, or it is explicitly neither — say
      which and why. Board 2 established that a diagram kind gains animation by tagging drawn
      elements with `data-siren-id`; a frame nobody can name is a decision, not an oversight.
- [ ] A graph with **no** subgraph lays out exactly as it does today. `layoutDirectedGraph`'s own
      comment says compound mode shifts routing, which is why it is conditional — assert that the
      existing placement is unchanged, because this is the regression that would be invisible.
- [ ] One corpus row moves to `supported`. Measured after ticket 02 landed (`c6b07fa`): the corpus
      stands at **57 supported / 14 rejected / 3 silently-wrong**. Expect `REJECTED` 14 → **13**;
      `SILENTLY_WRONG` stays 3 — none of its rows is this ticket's. These are an *expectation, not a
      quota*: if you find a further gap, add the row, say so, and let the number rise.

no-subgraph-unchanged claim; `render()` for the frame; the corpus.
